subject: Embeddings pricing, dims & discount request (DataWave)
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@datawave.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@datwave.ai
Date: 2026-06-29T15:12:00Z
Subject: Quick: embeddings pricing (dims / per-vector vs per-token)

Hi Lauren,

We are evaluating embedding costs for a rollout of semantic search and similarity features across DataWave's product suite. A few quick questions so we can build an internal TCO:  

- Do you price embeddings per-vector (e.g., per vector created) or per-token for the text input? Any options for both?
- What are the supported embedding dimensions (e.g., 768, 1536, other)? Can you serve multiple dims in the same contract?
- Which models do you recommend / support for production embeddings (open models + Redwood variants)?
- If we expect ~100M vectors/year, what volume discounts or committed pricing do you offer?

Can you send your current rate card and an indicative SOW for a 12 month pilot/rollout? Also, procurement will need SOC 2 evidence and basic legal terms.

Thanks — appreciate a ballpark so we can budget.

Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Search & ML
DataWave Analytics
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@datawave.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, procurement@datwave.ai
Date: 2026-06-29T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick: embeddings pricing (dims / per-vector vs per-token)

Hi Oliver — great to hear from you. High level answers and I've attached a short rate card + SOW draft. Happy to set up a call if you prefer to walk through numbers.

Baseline pricing (hosted Redwood embeddings):
- Per-vector pricing (recommended for most customers): 1536-dim model: $0.00040 / vector; 768-dim model: $0.00022 / vector.
- Per-token alternative (available as an option if you want end-to-end token billing tied to text inputs): roughly equivalent for typical document lengths, but per-vector is simpler for bulk storage/lookup.

Supported dims / models:
- Redwood-embed-1536 (recommended for high-quality semantic search & re-ranking)
- Redwood-embed-768 (cost-optimized for large-scale similarity / approximate recall)
- We also support community/open checkpoints on request (e.g., embedding variants comparable to ada/text-similarity), and Dedicated/private deployments can host custom dims.

Discounts / packaging:
- Volume tiers (published): 1M-10M, 10M-50M, 50M-200M with incremental % discounts.
- For large committed volume we offer committed-usage pricing (annual) with additional % off. Example: a 12-month commitment for 50M+/yr is eligible for 15–20% off list per-vector price.

For your stated ~100M vectors/yr, we can do a tailored proposal. Two quick options:
A) 12-month committed: 20% off list on the 1536-dim price (effective $0.00032/vector) with monthly billing.
B) Pilot -> commit: 60-day pilot at list, convert to annual commit within 45 days of pilot close and receive a retroactive credit of pilot charges up to 15%.

I've attached Redwood_RateCard_v2.pdf and a draft SOW (DW_Master_SOW_draft.docx) to seed the conversation.

Marissa (cc'ed) is our sales engineer — looping her in for dimensional tradeoffs and latency targets. Ben, can you confirm approval path for anything beyond the standard 20%?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@datawave.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, procurement@datwave.ai
Date: 2026-06-30T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick: embeddings pricing (dims / per-vector vs per-token)

Hi Oliver — quick technical notes to help with the sizing and pricing decision:

- Dimensionality tradeoffs: 1536 dims give better semantic fidelity and usually increase downstream reranking quality. 768 dims are ~40–55% cheaper (storage + per-vector cost) and often adequate for first-pass recall. We commonly recommend a two-pass pattern: 768 for recall + 1536 for re-rank on the top-k candidates.
- Storage & retrieval cost: remember to budget for vector store costs (we can host vectors or you can store in your vector DB). If you want Redwood-managed vector storage, we add a storage line item in the SOW (we included a conservative estimate in the pricing sheet).
- Throughput and batching: batching and optimized inference paths reduce per-vector compute cost in practice; we’ll size the pool based on your QPS sample.

If you can share expected mean document length (tokens) and desired 95th pct latency for lookup/re-rank, we can produce a tighter cost estimate and expected monthly token/vector counts.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-minute tech scoping call.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Lauren / Marissa. A few procurement items before we proceed:  

- DataWave is targeting ~100M vectors/yr. Given that scale, our internal goal is to get at least 30% off list or an equivalent committed rebate. Can Redwood meet that with a standard annual contract? If not, what are the levers (term length, commit size, prepay)?
- We’d like a 60-day pilot to validate quality. Would Redwood consider a pilot with billable usage at list rates and a retroactive concession if we convert to a 12-month commit?
- Please provide SOC 2 (Type II) evidence and standard DPIA compliance notes.
- Legal: our timeline is two weeks for commercial review + legal checks if terms are close to market.

We’ve attached DataWave_procurement_template.pdf (sent separately).

-Sara

DataWave Analytics

Sara / Oliver — thanks for the clarity. Responding to your points and proposing a path forward.

- Discount: we can offer a 25% discount on the 1536-dim per-vector list price (list $0.00040 -> $0.00030) in exchange for a 12-month committed minimum of 75M vectors/year (commit can be annualized; overage billed at discounted rate). For larger commits or prepay, we can increase the discount (we should discuss exact thresholds).
- Pilot: we agree to a 60-day pilot at list price; if you sign the 12-month commitment within 45 days of pilot close, we will apply a retroactive credit equal to up to 15% of pilot charges (this is in lieu of a full retroactive discount).
- SOC 2 / compliance: SOC 2 Type II report and DPIA summary are available — see the link in the rate card. I’ve attached an updated Redwood_RateCard_v2.pdf (page 3 has SOC 2 link) and an updated SOW with the commit option documented.
- Legal timeline: Ben (cc) is our commercial lead on approvals; Ben, is the 25% / 75M commit within our standard delegated approval or do you want to route to RevOps?

Next steps (recommended):
1) Confirm the 75M annual commit (or propose alternative threshold).
2) Exchange pilot statement of work and MSA redlines (we attached the SOW draft).
3) Schedule onboarding + scoping call (Marissa to run tech scoping).

If DataWave is comfortable with the 25%/75M starting point, I’ll get a formal quote out today and route the SOW to legal.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
